freeze_note: Hand-authored fixture missions for a fictional 'Acme' staging app. groundTruthTier is a human QA-lead judgment call about the minimum tier capable of doing the mission justice, made independently of the appraiser's own scoring vocabulary in src/routing/appraiser.ts — the point of the benchmark is to see how well an independently-scored mission brief lines up with that judgment, not to hand the appraiser a corpus written to its own keyword list. Do not edit missions in place; append a new corpus_version and add missions instead, so historical benchmark runs stay reproducible against the corpus they were run on.

missions.mission: Check that the marketing homepage loads and the primary "Sign up" button is visible and clickable.
Log in with the test account and confirm the dashboard greeting shows the user's name.
Open the pricing page and verify all three plan cards render with a price and a call-to-action button.
Click through the top navigation bar and confirm every link goes somewhere and none of them 404.
Verify the footer links (About, Contact, Privacy) open and load without errors.
Confirm the search box on the docs page accepts input and returns a results page.
Check the 404 page appears correctly when navigating to a made-up URL.
Verify the newsletter signup form on the homepage accepts an email address and shows a confirmation message.
Log in, create a new project from the dashboard, rename it, and confirm the rename is reflected in the project list.
Walk through the account settings flow: update the display name, change the avatar, and verify both changes persist after a page reload.
Add an item to the cart, adjust the quantity, remove a different item, and confirm the running total updates correctly at each step.
Create a support ticket with an attachment, then verify it appears in the ticket list with the correct status.
Invite a teammate by email, confirm the pending-invite state shows correctly, then simulate accepting it and check that the member list updates.
Test the multi-step onboarding wizard end to end: company info, team size, and integrations, and confirm the summary screen matches what was entered.
Filter the billing history table by date range and export type, and confirm the filtered rows match the applied filters.
Upload a CSV of contacts, confirm the import preview shows the right row count, then complete the import and check the contacts list.
Switch between two workspaces as the same user and confirm each workspace's data (projects, members) stays isolated from the other.
Test password reset: request a reset, follow the test-inbox stub's reset link, set a new password, and log in with it.

Test the checkout flow under a promo-code edge case: apply an expired code, apply a code below the minimum order value, then apply a valid one, and confirm the price recalculates correctly at each step with no stale total left over from the previous attempt.

Exercise the subscription downgrade flow: verify the prorated credit is calculated and shown before confirming, and confirm the downgrade doesn't take effect until the current billing period ends, per the account's billing page.

Open two tabs as the same logged-in user, edit the same project's settings in both, save in tab A first and then tab B, and confirm the app surfaces a conflict rather than silently overwriting tab A's change.
Test session-expiry handling: let the session token expire mid-flow while filling out a long form, then submit, and confirm the app prompts a re-login rather than silently dropping the form data.

Verify role-based access: as a 'member' role, confirm every admin-only action (billing, team removal, API key rotation) is either hidden or blocked with a clear permission error, not just visually disabled.

Trigger a webhook-driven status update (mark an external order as shipped) and confirm the in-app order status updates without a manual refresh, and that a second, duplicate webhook delivery doesn't double-apply the status change.
Test the bulk-delete flow on a list of fifty-plus items: select all, delete, and confirm pagination, counts, and any cached summary numbers elsewhere in the app all reconcile afterward.

Walk through the refund flow for a partially-shipped multi-item order: refund one item only, and confirm the remaining order total, shipping status, and the customer-facing order page all stay consistent.

Do a full exploratory pass across the entire application as a brand-new trial user: onboarding, every primary navigation section, billing, team management, integrations, and settings. Note anything inconsistent, broken, or confusing anywhere, including cross-page consistency issues such as a number that disagrees with itself on two different pages, and give comprehensive, full coverage rather than spot-checking.

Perform an end-to-end regression sweep across the areas changed in the last three releases: checkout, billing, team invites, and the new integrations marketplace, cross-referencing behavior against the in-app help docs for each, and flag any place the product no longer matches its own documentation.

In a tightly time-boxed pass, cover as much of the billing, subscription, and team-permissions surface as you can, prioritizing anything that touches money or access control, and be thorough rather than fast — this is the last check before a pricing change ships.

Explore the entire settings area end to end (account, security, notifications, billing, integrations, API keys, danger zone), testing every toggle and every destructive-looking action's confirmation dialog without actually completing anything destructive, and give full coverage of edge cases like disabling two-factor auth, rotating API keys, and downgrading to a plan with fewer seats than current members.
